extracted.intended_audience: individuals or entities seeking to file petitions (exemption, rulemaking, or reconsideration) with the FAA
extracted.subtask_short: FAA petition for exemption or rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and required contents for submitting petitions to the FAA seeking exemptions from regulations, requests for rulemaking, or petitions for reconsideration, including timing, substantive justifications, and supporting data expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 14 CFR Part 11
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitions must comply with 14 CFR Part 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural requirements such as timing (see the 120-day requirement below). Failure to provide a petition that includes all of the required information may result in the FAA taking no action on the petition and closing the petition without further notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — 120 days submission for exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must send a petition for exemption 120 days before you need the exemption to take effect or 120 days before your current exemption expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required by 14 CFR § 11.63(d). Plan submissions to allow FAA processing lead time; late petitions risk denial or inaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Exemption — petitioner contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Your name and mailing address and, if you wish, other contact information such as a fax number, telephone number, or e-mail address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, deliverable contact info so FAA can correspond and publish required summaries. Omitting contact information can impede processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Exemption — identify specific regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific section or sections of Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) from which you seek an exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite precise 14 CFR provision(s) so FAA can locate the exact regulatory requirement at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Exemption — state extent and reason for relief sought
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of relief you seek, and the reason you seek the relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as detailed as possible about what regulatory obligations you seek relief from and why partial vs. full relief is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Exemption — public interest justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The reasons why granting your request would be in the public interest; that is, how it would benefit the public as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain public benefits concretely (safety, efficiency, innovation, public convenience). The FAA evaluates exemptions against public interest considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Exemption — safety equivalence justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The reasons why granting the exemption would not adversely affect safety, or how the exemption would provide a level of safety at least equal to that provided by the rule from which you seek the exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address safety impacts directly with data, analysis, or operational mitigations. The FAA may grant an exemption only if it is in the public interest and provides an equivalent level of safety (see 49 U.S.C. § 44701(f) and 14 CFR § 11.81(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Exemption — Federal Register summary for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary we can publish in the Federal Register stating the rule from which you seek the exemption and a brief description of the nature of the exemption you seek.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise, publishable summary that accurately identifies the rule and the exemption sought; this text will be used for public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Exemption — additional supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional information, views or arguments available to support your request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include supporting documents, precedent exemptions, operational descriptions, test data, or other evidence. If you want to exercise privileges of your exemption outside the United States, state the reason why you need to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Rulemaking — petitioner contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Your name and mailing address and, if you wish, other contact information such as a fax number, telephone number, or e-mail address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with exemptions, provide reliable contact information so FAA can follow up and publish notices as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Rulemaking — explanation of proposed action and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of your proposed action and its purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state what regulatory change you want (adopt, amend, repeal) and the objectives it seeks to achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Rulemaking — proposed regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: The language you propose for a new or amended rule, or the language you would remove from a current rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise drafting of regulatory text changes rather than only conceptual descriptions; this helps FAA evaluate scope and drafting implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Rulemaking — public interest and supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of why your proposed action would be in the public interest, plus information and arguments that support your proposed action, including relevant technical and scientific data available to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with technical/scientific data, analysis, citations, and demonstrated facts or circumstances that show need for the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Rulemaking — facts, circumstances, and potential FAA-requested analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Any specific facts or circumstances that support or demonstrate the need for the action you propose. FAA may request information about costs/benefits, regulatory burdens, recordkeeping/reporting burdens, and environmental effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide cost-benefit information (including impacts on targeted or affected groups), analysis of regulatory burden on small entities and tribes, recordkeeping/reporting impacts, and effects on natural and social environments if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Reconsideration — timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA must receive your petition for reconsideration within 60 days after we issued the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing is mandatory; missing the 60-day window may preclude reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Reconsideration — required showing/grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Your petition for reconsideration must establish one of the following: (1) you have a significant additional fact and why you did not present it in your original petition; (2) that FAA made an important factual error in its denial; or (3) that FAA did not correctly interpret a law, regulation, or precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate which of the discrete grounds applies and provide supporting evidence or legal argument showing why reconsideration is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAA exemption grant standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA may grant an exemption if it is in the public interest and provides an equivalent level of safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the substantive test FAA applies when evaluating exemption petitions (statutory and regulatory citations: 49 U.S.C. § 44701(f); 14 CFR § 11.81(e)). Address both public interest and safety equivalence in the petition.
